surface_forms: un écrivain du nom de Bergotte

appraisal_events.evidence: Norpois calls Bergotte «un joueur de flûte», finds his books «sans muscles», «bien mièvre, bien mince, et bien peu viril», «des chinoiseries de forme», «des subtilités de mandarin déliquescent», and the man himself «plus prétentieux, plus solennel, moins homme de bonne compagnie», «un diseur de phébus», inferior to Vigny.
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois devotes the whole passage to an authoritative demolition of Bergotte as writer and as man, but the narration undercuts him: he speaks entirely in ready-made formulas («la charrue avant les bœufs», «un double flot de Barbares»), so the verdict lands as Norpois's diplomatic idiom rather than as endorsed judgment.

appraisal_events.evidence: «votre admiration tout à fait exagérée pour Bergotte», «j'aurais mauvaise grâce à ne pas passer l'éponge, puisque vous avez dit vous-même... que ce n'était qu'un griffonnage d'enfant», «vous n'êtes pas le seul qui se soit cru poète à son heure»; the narrator confesses that Norpois «m'inspira sur ma propre intelligence des doutes plus graves que ceux qui me déchiraient d'habitude».
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois extends condescending absolution to the boy's prose while faulting it for Bergotte's «mauvaise influence», and the narrator records real damage to his self-estimation; the parenthesis «(je l'avais dit, en effet, mais je n'en pensais pas un mot)» ironizes Norpois's magnanimity without cancelling the blow.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is locally crushed: what he placed «mille et mille fois au-dessus de moi-même» is ranked at the bottom by Norpois, his own writing is pardoned as a child's scribble, and he explicitly reports graver doubts about his intelligence.

Bergotte is comprehensively disparaged by the passage's only speaking authority, but the diminishment is softened by the ironic framing of the evaluator and by his own concession that «l'œuvre est infiniment supérieure à l'auteur».

Norpois holds the floor unchallenged; the mother and the timid boy merely feed him openings, and he alone dispenses literary verdicts and pardons, even if the narration quietly exposes his formulaic manner.

ambiguities: The narrator supplies no counter-argument to Norpois's verdict on Bergotte, so the diminishment could be read as neutrally reported; the ironizing reading rests on framing signals (Norpois's stock phrases, the disclosed lie about the «griffonnage d'enfant», the young narrator's disproportionate collapse) rather than on any explicit narratorial rebuttal.
